why.correct: Counts from groups of different sizes cannot be compared directly. Divide each part by its own whole and compare the decimals.

why.correct: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>÷</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \div 3 = 0.6667</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.6667</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>66.67</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6667 \times 100 = 66.67</annotation></semantics></math>, which rounds to 66.7%.

why.correct: The fraction bar acts like brackets: add the top first, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 + 4 + 9 = 15</annotation></semantics></math>, then divide, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{15}{3} = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

Inside first: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-3)^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (-1)^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 4^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 9</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 16</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 26</annotation></semantics></math>; the bottom is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - 1 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>26</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{26}{2} = 13</annotation></semantics></math>; then <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>13</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3.61</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{13} = 3.61</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum x_i</annotation></semantics></math> tells you to add every <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_i</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 + 5 + 10 = 18</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: The summation sign adds; it does not multiply.

Right: the summation sign adds every value, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 + 5 + 10 = 18</annotation></semantics></math>.
Dividing by 3 gives the average; the sum itself is 18.
That is how many terms there are, not their sum.

why.correct: Order of operations: brackets, powers and roots, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.
options: Left to right gives <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 \times 3</annotation></semantics></math>, but multiplication comes before addition.
The <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> sign asks for a product, not a sum.

why.correct: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12 + 15 + 18 + 21}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>66</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{66}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>16.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 16.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

A square is never negative: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-3)^2 = 9</annotation></semantics></math>. On a calculator, type the brackets, or <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3^2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-9</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-3) \times (-3) = 9</annotation></semantics></math>; a negative times a negative is positive.

That is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-(3^2)</annotation></semantics></math>. With the brackets, the whole <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math> is squared.
Squaring multiplies a number by itself, not by 2.

A square is a number times itself: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-3)(-3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: The square root of a number is the value that, times itself, gives the number: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>0.5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5^2 = 0.25</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: A square root undoes squaring; it does not halve.

Check: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.05</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0.05</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0025</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05 \times 0.05 = 0.0025</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0.25.

Right: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25</annotation></semantics></math>.
That squares 0.25 instead of taking its root.

why.correct: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mfrac><mn>26</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>13</mn></msqrt><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.61</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\frac{26}{2}} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.61</annotation></semantics></math>. The brackets of the root hold the whole fraction.

Substitute, then follow the order: top first, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62 - 50 = 12</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{12}{8} = 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: That works out <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>50</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62 - \frac{50}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>. The fraction bar groups <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62 - 50</annotation></semantics></math> first.
Substitute 62 for x, subtract 50, then divide by 8.

Right: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{62 - 50}{8} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

The formula is x minus 50, so <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>62</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62 - 50 = 12</annotation></semantics></math>, which is positive.

why.correct: Brackets, then powers, then the sum on top, then the division, and the square root of the whole result last.

Each term is a signed distance from 5: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>, which add to 0. Here 5 is the average, and distances from the average always add to 0.

Squaring is a different formula, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum (x_i - 5)^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Signs count: the distances below 5 are negative.
The 5 is subtracted from each value before adding.

why.correct: "At least 3" is 3 or more: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X \ge 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: That is "more than 3", which leaves out 3.

why.correct: "Fewer than 3" means <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo><</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X < 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
